summary:
Sentinel is an autonomous crew health and environmental monitoring web platform designed for long-duration 120-day space missions. Built using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with complete English and Spanish support, it provides real-time tracking of vital signs and cabin telemetry, utilizing NASA RadLab data to benchmark environmental radiation exposure.

Sentinel addresses the critical challenge of astronaut health management and high communication latency during deep-space exploration. By functioning entirely offline, it empowers crews with autonomous oversight, early warning indicators, and robust telemetry analysis when connection to Earth is disrupted.

This project is vital because safeguarding human health is paramount for sustainable space exploration. Furthermore, Sentinel’s offline-first resilience features valuable terrestrial dual-use potential, making it adaptable for extreme, isolated environments on Earth, such as remote scientific and Arctic outposts.
details:
Project Details: Sentinel

  • What it does & How it works:
    Sentinel is a lightweight, web-based crew health and environmental monitoring platform engineered specifically for simulated 120-day deep-space missions. It functions as an autonomous dashboard that tracks vital signs, cabin telemetry, and environmental metrics. By integrating open data and benchmarks from NASA RadLab, the system evaluates radiation dosage equivalents and cabin parameters ($CO_2$ levels, life support status) in real time. Built with an offline-first architecture, Sentinel operates seamlessly without requiring a constant connection to Earth, ensuring continuous functionality during deep-space communication blackouts. It also features a built-in localization module (i18n.js) supporting instant English and Spanish toggling for multinational crews.
    • Autonomy & Reliability: Empowers astronauts with immediate, local oversight of health anomalies and environmental hazards without relying on mission control delay loops.
    • Mission Safety: Reduces cognitive load under high-stress isolated conditions through an intuitive, clean interface and early warning indicators.
    • Terrestrial Dual-Use Potential: Beyond space exploration, Sentinel’s robust offline resilience makes it highly adaptable for extreme, isolated environments on Earth, such as remote Arctic research outposts, high-altitude stations, or deep-sea expeditions.
    • Frontend & Logic: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript.
      • Development Workflow: Iteratively developed with transparent AI assistance (utilizing ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) for code structuring, debugging, and documentation refinement.
